findings.text: Diamond Rapids-X (family 19, model 1): ISA predicted by gcc PTA_DIAMONDRAPIDS, not read from CPUID: AVX10.2, APX_F, AMX-FP8, AMX-FP16, AMX-COMPLEX, AMX-AVX512, AMX-MOVRS, MOVRS — fallback model table: CPUID is not readable here (sudo k3d-gpu doctor reads /dev/cpu/0/cpuid; needs the cpuid module); /proc/cpuinfo may not show these (kernel-dependent); NFD labels what CPUID reports (cpu-cpuid.AVX10_VERSION, APX_F, AMXFP8) and oneDNN/OpenVINO pick them with no flag
AMX (amx_bf16 amx_int8 amx_tile) — CPU instructions, usable in any pod; up labels nodes feature.node.kubernetes.io/cpu-cpuid.AMX*
CPU ISA: AVX512BF16 AVX512F AVX512VNNI AVXVNNI — up labels nodes feature.node.kubernetes.io/cpu-cpuid.<name>=true (NFD names)
DSA: 8 device(s), 2 user work queue(s) — deployed by 'k3d-gpu up' (intel-dsa-plugin)
IAA: 8 device(s), 2 user work queue(s) — deployed by 'k3d-gpu up' (intel-iaa-plugin)

NUMA: 6 node(s) (6 with CPUs), SNC 3 per L3, 2 socket(s) — up deploys the NRI balloons policy; label pods k3d-gpu.io/cores=replica for a balloon inside one NUMA node, memory pinned to it, near the pod's devices

RDT allocation (rdt_a: cat_l3 cdp_l3 mba) — resctrl classes are available but left off: the balloons policy ships control.rdt.enable: false because enabling it rewrites the host's /sys/fs/resctrl. To opt in, mount resctrl on the host (mount -t resctrl resctrl /sys/fs/resctrl) and set control.rdt.enable: true in nri-balloons.yml; usePodQoSAsDefaultClass then gives BestEffort/Burstable/Guaranteed pods 33%/66%/100% of the L3

noisy-neighbour isolation: rdt-mba — CAT + MBA can cap a neighbour's cache share and DRAM bandwidth through the RDT opt-in above (resctrl mounted: no); the shipped classes set cache shares only, so add mbAllocation: {all: ["50%"]} to the BestEffort class for bandwidth; the classes run inside the NRI balloons policy, which up deploys on hybrid or multi-NUMA hosts only
per socket: socket 0: DSA 4, IAA 4, QAT 0; socket 1: DSA 4, IAA 4, QAT 0 (no ARK default on file for this CPU)

findings.text: no cpufreq policy exposed (VM or cpufreq disabled) — nothing to tune here
uncore00: max_freq_khz 1800000 is below the hardware ceiling 2200000
findings.why: a lowered uncore ceiling caps ring/LLC (client) or mesh and memory-controller (Xeon) clock, and token generation reads every weight once per token through it

findings.text: /dev/kvm present: microVM sandboxes (Kata, Firecracker) can run here

findings.apply: sudo modprobe -r kvm_intel && sudo modprobe kvm_intel tdx=1
findings.revert: sudo modprobe -r kvm_intel && sudo modprobe kvm_intel tdx=0
findings.text: the CPU reports tdx_host_platform but kvm_intel runs without TDX (tdx=N): no confidential microVM sandboxes
findings.why: kvm_intel creates TDX guests only when loaded with tdx=1; stop running VMs and microVM sandboxes first, since modprobe -r kvm_intel fails while one holds /dev/kvm

findings.apply: BIOS: enable VT-d, then add intel_iommu=on to the kernel command line and reboot
findings.revert: remove intel_iommu=on from the kernel command line and reboot
findings.text: no IOMMU unit registered: no DMA isolation between devices, no GPU passthrough into a microVM
findings.why: VFIO hands a device to a VM only with its IOMMU group; without VT-d enabled there are no groups

sections.good: cores ramp to full turbo the moment a request arrives: EPP performance or balance_performance, turbo on, no frequency caps — token generation is a latency-bound loop and every ramp-up shows in time-to-first-token
sections.name: CPU frequency (driver none)

sections.good: max_freq_khz at initial_max_freq_khz and min_freq_khz at initial_min_freq_khz: the hardware (UFS, or ELC on TPMI parts) picks the uncore clock inside the full range. A floor pinned high for decode is unproven (EXPERIMENTS.md H29, INCONCLUSIVE), so it is not suggested
